scenes.text: China's 2015 crash began with a vertical climb. The Shanghai Composite rose roughly one hundred and fifty percent into June. Easy money was the story. Borrowed cash was the fuel.
Borrowing magnifies a gain. But it leaves the investor's own money as a thin layer underneath. When prices slip, collateral shrinks first. Cross the threshold, and positions are sold.
Now the loop closes. Forced sales hit the order book. Prices fall, more accounts breach limits, and more shares meet thinner bids. Selling does not just reflect the fall. It creates the next one.

Authorities added liquidity and state-backed buying. That can slow the machine. But it cannot instantly create willing buyers. Leverage makes confidence the scarce asset. When it breaks, the feedback loop does the rest.
